evidence:
Authority and identity: I read the actual frozen XLSX with openpyxl: rules/WebDev Rubrics QC.xlsx, Quality Checks sheet row 22 (quality number 21), says test.sh must launch safely, gate on liveness, run gates before scored with score.py after each, and write a reward on every code path. I also read Internal Quality Checks row 22 and Deterministic Checks rows 7, 33 and 36. The matching frozen skill quality-checks.md:92-94 requires unprivileged launch, symlink escape refusal, early zero reward and ensured exits; staged-task-contract.md:98-111 describes the ordered contract. Current qc/REVIEW_POLICY.md requires distinguishing source, scripted product observations and full verifier evidence. T below denotes .qc-cache/coldwater-2026-09-30-hardening/task. The manifest input is a6a5219e9c5aa5e19c2b30acb01ca3a1719938a02ea09674cd18e08987bf43a9. Actual file hashes match manifest entries for test.sh, score.py, restart_mcp.py, workbook, skill and all three cited references.

Positive source findings and error-path audit: T/tests/test.sh:14-23 defines complete plain-zero outputs and nonempty-file fallback; lines 60-61 write zero and install the EXIT cleanup before checking judge variables, server.js or submission symlinks. Missing judge/model (63-66), missing entry (68-70), rejected symlink (72-83), copy/permission/setup errors under set -e (90-95), startup readiness failure (115-125), restart-helper/prompt preparation error (127-201), gates-suite nonzero/timeout (203-215), and scored-suite nonzero/timeout (224-226) therefore already have zero reward files. Lines 72-83 reject links outside the allowed node_modules tree; 104-111 launch through setsid, env -i and UID/GID 65534. Readiness probes occur before RewardKit. Lines 212-227 clear old scored output, run gates, call score.py, preserve the detailed zero on true gate failure, overwrite with plain zero for scorer errors, then run scored and score.py again. A scored-suite failure retains the gate-only aggregate, whose reward is still zero; it need not imply missing output. score.py:35-60 explicitly gives zero when scored data is absent; validates finite numeric dimensions (13-20); exceptions return 2 (86-91), which the caller handles. No shell exec replaces the trapped process; find -exec at line 86 is not that prohibited construct. Successful scoring preserves its nonempty files through ensure_reward. Bash syntax validation of this exact frozen test.sh returned 0; both shared Python tools parsed successfully. These are source/parser observations, not an end-to-end verifier run.

Credible inherited defect 1, unsafe restart success: T/tests/test.sh:152-159 sends TERM and polls the old process group 50 times, but after exhausting that loop it continues with no failure or KILL. Lines 160-169 launch a replacement and overwrite app.pid. Lines 170-183 decide success solely from probe_ready; there is no kill -0 check of the new PID, no assurance the old group died, and no attribution of the responding listener. probe_ready at 130-145 accepts any HTTP response from port 3000, including HTTPError. Thus the existing still-running listener can supply the response while the replacement has failed with EADDRINUSE. T/tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:restart translates helper exit 0 into the explicit claim 'the server was relaunched on the same database and answers HTTP'. The functional prompt relies on that completion at T/tests/scored/functional/prompt.md:23 and 363-369, and criterion cw_process_restart_durability at judge.toml:347-351 awards actual process-restart survival. A false helper success can therefore award survival without process replacement. This is a direct control-flow counterexample, not a regex heuristic or a claim that the current golden earned a wrong score.

Credible inherited defect 2, unbounded cleanup: T/tests/test.sh:33-40 performs 'kill -- -"$APP_PID"' and then 'wait "$APP_PID"' before ensure_reward, without a deadline or forced termination. A launched child that remains alive after TERM can stall this EXIT trap indefinitely. The prewritten zero or already computed reward generally remains present: this finding DOES NOT establish that a reward is absent. Its demonstrated source consequence is unbounded verifier termination and failure to reach the final ensure_reward call; the eventual host-timeout treatment is unmeasured. After restart overwrites app.pid with a dead replacement, cleanup also loses its reference to a surviving old group.

Inherited-template constraint: byte comparisons found the frozen task and frozen template test.sh identical, SHA256 bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa; score.py also identical (13de2b3885967e22aa13ded3bf33c354e3e741e85be871612c04e996eef5c04e) and restart_mcp.py identical (03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5). These defects are inherited harness conflicts, not unauthorized task-specific drift. The shared-template preservation rule prevents silently fixing them in this review.

Executed evidence and its limits: golden/run-golden-20260930-070504/RESULTS.json and actual-restart.json record one successful ordinary restart, PID 16 to 335, 5.645670579979196 seconds; the earlier 070305 run records 16 to 336. Both name the canonical MCP hash above and helper-template hash 0db23e8c7c8d70c7e934c4d13ccbb2326a4da2cb47f1b2ba1967009d829be3b7, which I independently derived from the frozen heredoc. The 070504 saved-record/read-write facts after restart passed. Its executed drivers/launch_workflow.py:38 launches the server separately; 59-64 extract only the helper; 69-72 call MCP and additionally await the original server exit; 85-91 implement separate Python cleanup. It does NOT execute the full canonical test.sh, its EXIT trap, RewardKit gates/scored suites, or score.py. No resistant-process, replacement-failure or canonical error-path run is present in those observations. The normal successful restart does not refute either source counterexample. The full configured judge, Oracle score and behavior under the listed adverse paths remain unmeasured. No new Docker/provider run was performed.
counterexample: Source-derived, not executed in this audit. False pass: a Node server holds its saved library in memory, accepts independent-browser saves/readbacks and registers process.on('SIGTERM', () => {}); its existing listener survives the helper's five-second poll. The replacement cannot bind port 3000, but the old listener answers the helper's HTTP probe. MCP reports restart completion, the original memory still serves the records and later saves, and the restart-survival criterion can pass without a process restart. Conforming alternative at risk of false failure: a correct SQLite-backed app implements an eight-second graceful SIGTERM shutdown, which the public integration contract does not prohibit. The same helper can claim completion from that old listener after five seconds while its replacement fails to bind; the old process subsequently exits and downstream browser checks lose the otherwise conforming service. Cleanup witness: an otherwise functional server with a retained TERM handler can keep the EXIT trap at the unbounded wait, even though its initialized reward files still exist.
suggested_fix: Escalate the inherited conflict to the shared harness owner rather than changing task-controlled settings. In a newly authorized canonical candidate, bound process-group shutdown, verify old-group death and replacement PID liveness before accepting HTTP readiness, and ensure reward preservation plus original exit status survive bounded cleanup. Measure the exact canonical entrypoint against ordinary and TERM-resistant apps, children, a replacement that exits, suite/scorer failures and both zero/nonzero preexisting rewards; retain the current normal-restart evidence only by matching hashes.
